Prepare a data frame for boundary logic analysis

bl_prepare_data.Rd

Converts a multiclass or binary class column to a numeric 0/1 indicator, selects feature columns, produces a reproducible train/test split, and removes outliers from the training set using a convex hull polygon filter. Outlier filtering is integrated: pass hull_fraction to control how aggressively the hull trims the outermost training points (default 0.9 removes approximately the outermost 10%).

Usage

bl_prepare_data(
  data,
  class_col,
  target_class = NULL,
  feature_cols = NULL,
  train_fraction = 0.8,
  seed = 121L,
  hull_fraction = 0.9,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

class_col

Character scalar; name of the column holding class labels.

target_class

The value in class_col that should be coded as 1. All other values become 0. If NULL, the column must already be numeric 0/1.

feature_cols

Character vector of column names to use as features. If NULL (default), all columns except class_col are used.

train_fraction

Numeric in (0, 1); proportion of rows allocated to training. Default 0.8.

seed

Integer; random seed for the train/test split. Default 121.

hull_fraction

Numeric in (0, 1]; fraction argument for the convex hull polygon filter applied to training data. Values below 1 trim the most extreme points; 1 retains all points. Default 0.9.

verbose

Logical; if TRUE, prints a one-line summary of rows retained and removed by the hull filter. Default TRUE.

Value

A list of class "bl_filter_result" with components:

train_data

Filtered training data frame with columns var_names + "class" (numeric 0/1).

test_data

Data frame of test rows, same structure (not filtered).

var_names

Character vector of feature column names.

num_vars

Integer; number of features.

target_class

The value that was mapped to 1, or NULL if no conversion was applied.

polygon

SpatialPolygons convex hull in standardised PCA space.

hull_fraction

The fraction value used for the hull filter.

n_retained

Number of training rows retained after filtering.

n_removed

Number of training rows removed by the filter.

Multiclass to binary conversion

If your data has more than two classes (e.g., datasets::iris has three Species), supply target_class to specify which class maps to 1. All other classes map to 0. For example:

# datasets::iris: treat "versicolor" as the positive class
bl_prepare_data(datasets::iris, class_col = "Species", target_class = "versicolor")

If target_class = NULL, the class column must already be numeric 0/1.

Examples

# Binary class, versicolor vs rest, default hull filter (0.9)
bl_dat <- bl_prepare_data(datasets::iris,
                           class_col    = "Species",
                           target_class = "versicolor",
                           hull_fraction = 0.9)
#> Hull fraction: 0.90 | Retained: 110 (91.7%) | Removed: 10 (8.3%)
cat(bl_dat$n_retained, "training rows retained\n")
#> 110 training rows retained
